Ten questions were dropped at render for sharing more vocabulary with another variant passage than their own. SSAT could not render: N variants give exactly N options and SSAT is 5-choice, so it needs a 5-variant re-author. KNOWN CONSTRAINT: items within a topic are non-independent (one shown variant answers all of them) — assembly must draw at most ONE item per topic per form; see READING-WORLDS-RESULT.md.

elimination.verdict: Hunter exploitable=false. It reconstructed the variant axis from options but could state no key-predicting rule; length, moderation and concreteness all tested flat. Its risk-1 (per-topic key-letter collapse) checked and cleared.

spec.method: symmetric worlds + KILL SPANS: each variant carries a verbatim span positively refuting every sibling answer (READING-WORLDS-S3-PREREGISTERED.md)

batches.note: Yield 93.6% (73 of 78) against a pre-registered 60% line; s2 was 36%. Gates: blind −9.7 (ctl 20.0), set-attack −5.4, pattern hunter exploitable=false over ~45 rules, with-passage QC 77/78 unanimous, cross-variant 75/78, 1320/1320 kill spans verbatim. Dropped 5, four of them the same shape - a short span aimed at a compound option, landing on a component the option survives losing. The 3 cross-variant failures were 3/3 with the key in the QC vote; dropped anyway rather than adjudicate between disagreeing instruments. LIMITATION: all six keys in a topic come from one variant, so effective n is TOPICS not items - spread forms across topics and do not score restatement pairs together.

spec.method: hand-authored, solve-gated: every item carries a JS solve body re-executed against its own key

batches.note: ISEE math 85 -> 130 against an 84-item form, so a second maths section is servable. Attack margin -1.5 (34.1% vs 35.6% control), attack file asserted stem-free. Two attacker hypotheses measured: sum-relation REFUTED (key is the summed value in 2 of 10 such sets); magnitude-rank REAL (options print ascending, key sits at rank 1 in 40.5% vs 25% expected) but neutralised by shuffleDrawnChoices at serve. Do not preserve ascending order for fidelity before rebalancing that skew - see IM4-RESULT.md.

shape.verdict: 45/45 solve bodies re-executed and matched their key by an independent evaluator. 4 distinct choices, key present, 3 named distractor mis-steps, 45 unique subskills. Options-only shape guards scoped to all-numeric sets: key is the lone perfect square in 1 of 42 (chance).

withsource.verdict: No human pass yet - this cohort is part of B5, the cofounder sweep over the SSAT/ISEE bank.

tells.verdict: Key letters A10/B16/C10/D9. Because options print ascending, letter spread IS magnitude-rank spread; recorded in IM4-RESULT.md rather than treated as a letter tell.

spec.method: hand-authored synonyms and analogies to a fixed distractor taxonomy (opposite / reversal / near-field / wrong-member)

batches.note: KILLED on the blind attack: solver 1 scored 80% from options alone, mean 48.0% vs 20.0% control, margin +28.0. Solver 3 scored 0/25, meaning odd-one-out is perfectly ANTI-correlated with the key - a second tell. Mechanism: every item carries a polar pair (antonym for synonyms, order-reversal for analogies) and the key is one of the two, 25 of 25, so three of five options are eliminable without the stem. The BRIEF caused it - an opposite-of-the-key distractor is recognisable only by reference to the key. Same shape as cr-v1. Not patched and re-run; see SV4-KILLED.md.

elimination.verdict: Three of five options eliminable with no stem in 25 of 25 items.

withsource.verdict: Not run - the batch was condemned before any with-source work was spent on it.

tells.verdict: Polar-pair prevalence 100%. Odd-one-out anti-correlation 0/25.

spec.method: hand-authored, solve-gated; 5 options with 4 named distractor mis-steps

batches.note: Shipped 19 of 25. SSAT math 77 -> 96 against a 50-item requirement. The AGGREGATE MARGIN HID the defect: whole batch +9.3, but the five items the attacker named before scoring came in at 73.3% against 20% chance while the other 20 sat at 33.3%. Cause: distractor sets built by iterating ONE operation on a seed (a doubling ladder, a radius-vs-diameter family), so the ladder is visible without the stem and the key is the middle rung. Authoring rule: the four distractors must come from DIFFERENT operations. Also recorded: with ascending numeric options and a key that is never rank 5, the key-letter spread check and the rank check measure the same thing, so a clean letter spread is weaker evidence than it looks. See SM4-RESULT.md.

shape.verdict: 25/25 solve bodies re-executed and matched their key by an independent evaluator. 5 distinct choices, key present, 4 named mis-steps. Shape guards applied to the 19 all-numeric sets; algebraic option sets excluded because parsing them invents false alarms.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack on the shipped 19: mean 33.3% vs 26.3% control, margin +7.0. The unfiltered 25 scored +9.3, which was a passing number over a broken subset.

elimination.verdict: Six items dropped: five named by the attacker as isolable from options alone (confirmed at 73.3%) plus SM4-11, whose coordinate options (3,-4) and (6,-8) are mutually incriminating.

withsource.verdict: No human pass yet; part of register item B5.

tells.verdict: Key letters on the shipped 19 spread with a 26.3% control. NOTE: on an ascending-order numeric bank the letter check is not independent of the magnitude-rank check.

spec.method: hand-authored, solve-gated; authored to FLATTEN the magnitude-rank skew measured on isee-math-s4

batches.note: Attack margin +3.0 (29.6% vs 26.7% control). ISEE math 130 -> 174 against an 84-item form, comfortably two sections. The rank fix WORKED: s4 had the key at magnitude rank 1 in 40.5% against 25% expected; s5 measures 9/11/13/9, and the attacker fixed-rank solver degenerated to always-C at 24.4%, which is chance. Dropped IM5-30, whose options included "3 : 5" and "6 : 10" - the SAME ratio, so neither could be the key. Found by a blind attacker rather than a checker, because every distinct-choices guard here compares STRINGS.

shape.verdict: 45/45 solve bodies re-executed and matched their key independently. 4 distinct choices, key present, 3 named mis-steps, 45 subskills with zero reuse from s4. The author mutation-tested its own checker with 12 planted faults, all of which fired, and caught a float mismatch (9.600000000000001 vs 9.6) that reading would have passed.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, prompt withheld because for maths the prompt IS the stem: mean 29.6% vs 26.7% control, margin +3.0. The four items the attacker named as leaky scored exactly at chance.

elimination.verdict: No roundness, digit-count, decimal-form, unit-format or option-length tell. The rank rule that paid on s4 no longer pays.

withsource.verdict: No human pass yet; part of register item B5.

tells.verdict: Key magnitude rank 9/11/13/9. New guard check-equivalent-options.mjs run over all 4,679 live items: 0 defects outside this batch.

spec.method: symmetric worlds + kill spans, authored against the s4 odd-category failure: all four answers to a question must be the same KIND of claim

batches.note: Yield 92.6% (50 of 54). ISEE reading 48 -> 75 drawable against a 36-item section, so it now serves two forms. Attack margin -19.8 with every item POSITION below chance. The attacker predicted, before scoring, that vocabulary items would be free marks lifting the batch above chance; measured, they scored 14.8%, the second-weakest position. Agreement among solvers is not evidence about the key. Four cross-variant failures in two NEW shapes: a kill that reverses an event direction rather than denying the event (I08-1, I08-2), and a kill contradicted by the variant own keyed sentence (I03-5, I08-5). The three s4 shapes are absent, which is the brief working. RENDERER WARNING: variant index is confounded with content in the source (W1 the unqualified endorsement 7 of 9, W4 the small-consequence stance 6 of 9 - the reviewer said 9 of 9 and overstated it). The seeded shuffle of shown variant and option order is the only thing keeping it out of the served item, so that shuffle is load-bearing.

shape.verdict: 648/648 kill spans verbatim; keyword parity clean after the author repaired 8 hits caused by its own length edits; length ratios 1.019-1.058; blind file asserted passage-free.

nosource.verdict: mean 13.6% vs 33.3% control, margin -19.8. Scored per item POSITION as the attacker asked, since a pooled figure would hide a leak in one position: all six below chance.

elimination.verdict: The assert-then-deny paragraph shape does not reach the options - no negation, hedge or concessive in any option, and option order is re-permuted across items. The recurring stance position is a template present in every set, so membership identifies nothing.

withsource.verdict: Cross-variant reviewer read ALL 648 spans, no sampling: 50 of 54 pass. The author same-category claim verified per topic - clean for 5, loose for 3, materially false for I08 Q1/Q2, and the loose/false topics are exactly the ones that failed.

tells.verdict: Key letters spread across all four for every shown variant, because the renderer shuffles. See the renderer warning in the note.

spec.method: BIJECTIVE SETS - five (stem, answer) rows per topic, each answer correct for exactly one stem, seeded RNG picks the shown stem after text freeze. The cr-v7 provenance cure transferred to verbal.

batches.note: SSAT verbal 101 -> 124 against a 60-item section: 2.07 forms, up from 1.68. Pre-registered bars both MET: margin -5.6 against <= +10, best single solver 23.3% against <= 40%. The same section previous batch was killed the same day at +28.0 with a solver at 80%. Dropped 7 for EXCLUSIVITY, not guessability: 5 synonym sets on the evaluative twin (two words for the same behaviour differing only in approval, which a gloss cannot carry) and 2 analogy sets on nesting relation families. Both reviewers independently derived the same rule: narrowing one member protects only the direction you narrowed. Repair by replacing a member, never by re-wording a gloss. See EVALUATIVE-TWIN.md.

shape.verdict: 15 synonym + 15 analogy topics; 75 distinct stems and 75 distinct sources; zero collisions against the live bank; zero reversal pairs anywhere. The analogy author used a cyclic block design so all 15 relation families appear exactly 5 times with no repeated combination.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, stem withheld because for verbal the stem IS the question: mean 21.1% vs 26.7% control, margin -5.6, best solver 23.3%. Three distinct pick-strings.

elimination.verdict: The attacker found polar pairs still present in 14 of 15 synonym items but they no longer point at the key - they are a by-product of five glosses from one field and come in bunches, where the killed batch had exactly one manufactured from the key. It declined to report this as a finding.

withsource.verdict: Exclusivity review of all 300 synonym and 300 analogy off-diagonal cells: 7 topics FAIL. This is the gate the attack cannot see - an item whose distractor is also true has two correct answers.

tells.verdict: Key spread A8/B8/C3/D6/E5 before drops. No option string repeats across the batch; relation families do not sit at fixed letters.

spec.method: hand-authored, solve-gated; four distractors from FOUR DIFFERENT operations, never one operation iterated

batches.note: Attack margin +8.3 (33.3% vs 25.0% control), best solver 41.7%. SSAT math 96 -> 108 against a 50-item section, closing the last gap: EVERY delivered section of both tests now clears two full forms. Written against the defect that dropped six items from s4 - distractor sets built by iterating ONE operation on a seed, so the ladder and therefore the key were visible without the question. The attacker enumerated every pairwise relation across all 12 sets and found no chain of one operation through three or more options; the longest runs are two-member pairs. UNRESOLVED, recorded rather than acted on: the attacker proposed a HUB pattern - four distractors from four different operations still leak if all four derive FROM the key, making it the unique referenced value (SM5-02, SM5-06, SM5-12). Measured 33.3% against 20% chance on 9 picks, which is not significant at that size. Worth re-testing when the cohort is larger; the fix would be to relate some distractors to each other or to an intermediate quantity rather than all to the key. n=12 is small and the attacker said so itself, declining to trust any accuracy figure at that size and trusting only the ladder finding, which is arithmetic and was checked exhaustively rather than sampled.

shape.verdict: 12/12 solve bodies re-executed and matched their key independently. 5 distinct choices, key present, 4 named mis-steps, 12 subskills with zero reuse from s4, no two options sharing a value. The author caught three items that had drifted into ladders during authoring and repaired them, and found a bug in its own checker (the chain builder cycled on factor -1, reporting a plus-minus pair as a 7-long chain).

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, prompt withheld: mean 33.3% vs 25.0% control, margin +8.3.

elimination.verdict: No single-operation ladder anywhere, verified exhaustively over all pairwise relations. No rank rule pays; key rank spread D3/C3/E2/B2/A2 is flat.

withsource.verdict: No human pass yet; part of register item B5.

tells.verdict: The attacker noted that because numeric options print ascending, the key-letter spread and the key-RANK spread are the same statistic - so a flat letter spread here is one fact, not two.

gateVersionNote: v2 = 2026-08-01, when thresholds were calibrated against 183 published items. Any pass recorded under v1 is STALE, not Ready — the bar moved in both directions that day.
coverageNote: qualityTasks lists EVERY audited cohort making up the row. The two SAT rows each cover four College Board domains that were measured separately and disagree — judging the row by one of them counted 848 passing math items as failed. Cohort n values sum exactly to the row items, so readiness is attributed per cohort, not per row.
